claims.text: The baseline is an as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a conventional metal substrate.
The baseline coating has a coarse or intermediate grain size and a typical phase distribution and residual-stress state.
A controlled pre-treatment such as changing deposition parameters can refine the coating microstructure and increase grain-boundary density.
Pre-annealing is a possible route for refining this coating and increasing its grain-boundary density.
Dynamic recrystallization is active under the intended high-temperature sliding conditions.
Grain-boundary sliding is active under the intended high-temperature sliding conditions.
Greater grain-boundary area promotes dynamic grain refinement during deformation.
A refined microstructure promotes a more uniform strain distribution.
Increasing grain-boundary density enhances grain-boundary sliding during elevated-temperature sliding.
Increasing grain-boundary density enhances dynamic recrystallization during sliding.
Grain-boundary-mediated deformation and dynamic recrystallization shift deformation from localized shear to homogeneous plasticity.
The refined microstructure suppresses localized shear bands, twinning, or dislocation-channel networks.
More homogeneous deformation reduces stress concentrations.
Reduced stress concentration and homogeneous deformation lower wear relative to the coarse-grained state.
The coarse-grained coating is more prone to extreme shear localization than the refined coating.
Under identical high-temperature sliding conditions, the pre-treated grain-refined coating will have a lower wear rate than the baseline coating.
Under identical high-temperature sliding conditions, the pre-treated coating will show homogeneous plastic deformation rather than localized shear bands.
The predicted grain-boundary-mediated benefit may not occur at lower temperatures because thermal activation is insufficient.
